title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity of the all-solid-state battery.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ceramic ion conductor in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 250 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LATP material. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3InCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The LATP, LLZO, and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 40% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and electrochemical window of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more is described. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a styrene-butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

11. The method of claim 9, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The LLZO, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 6 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium bromide solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure for lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and tin substitution for improved moisture stability
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid is a crystallized glass comprising a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 75:25 in which 2 mol% to 6 mol% of the phosphorus is substituted by tin, and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated from the matrix. A glassy precursor prepared by melt quenching at 750 degrees C is reheated at 240 degrees C to 280 degrees C so that the beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 100 nm and a degree of crystallinity of 50% to 75%. The tin, a soft acid, binds the sulfur more strongly than phosphorus, and the cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 60 minutes is 8 cm3/g or less. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and retains 80% or more of the conductivity after the exposure. Unlike crystalline Li7P3S11 or Li6PS5Cl powders, the remaining vitreous phase gives good deformability, and an all-solid-state battery using the material shows improved cycle life.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 80 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.3 MPa or more. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and cycle life of the layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and cycle life and simpler handling.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
claims: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.
2. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more.
4. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers.
5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.2 micrometers to 4 micrometers.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the core particles are secondary particles having an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 6, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.
8. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
9. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6.9 nm to 10.7 nm.
10. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.

11. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
14. The method of claim 13, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
15. The method of claim 11, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
16. The method of claim 15, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 30% or less, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.

10. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the sheet is laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step.
11. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1.
12. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

17. The method of claim 14, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
18. The method of claim 17, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
19. The method of claim 14, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
20. The method of claim 14, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
21. The method of claim 20, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of erbium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 75% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. Specific examples are Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.

7. The free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more.

10. The free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, wherein the binder is at least one selected from the group consisting of PTFE, a PTFE copolymer, and ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene.

11. A method for producing the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ceramic ion conductor powder with 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
14. The method of claim 13, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

16. The method of claim 11, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
