title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The resulting LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved sinterability and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes for lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The content of Li2O is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the electrochemical window of the product.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode comprises an inorganic layer of silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The Ag-C layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The Ag-C layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP material. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The resulting Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the grain boundary resistance and sinterability of the cell.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An argyrodite ion-conductive solid represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the sinterability.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sheet thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state lithium battery using it. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The Li2ZrO3 and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. With zirconium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The content of P2O5 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The sheet thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 1.4 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the sheet formability and ionic conductivity of the layer.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a magnesium-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a magnesium additive. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved electrochemical window and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Argyrodite solid electrolyte with a lithium-rich surface composition matched to niobate-coated positive electrode active materials
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for use in a positive electrode mixture together with a coated positive electrode active material has an argyrodite crystal structure and a bulk composition represented by Li6PS5Cl, and a surface region having a thickness of 3 nm to 20 nm in which the lithium to phosphorus atomic ratio is 7.0 to 8.5, higher than the bulk ratio of 6.0, as determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The surface region, formed by treating the fired powder with lithium ethoxide in ethanol and drying at 150 degrees C to 200 degrees C, matches the lithium chemical potential of a lithium niobate coating layer on the active material so that lithium depletion at the coating interface and the resulting space-charge layer are suppressed. The solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C, and a positive electrode mixture containing the solid electrolyte and niobate-coated LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 shows an interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V of 25 ohm cm2 or less, 40% lower than that of an untreated argyrodite. The surface region also lowers the hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air by 30% or more, and an all-solid-state battery using the mixture shows improved cycle life; Li10GeP2S12 type conductors can be treated in the same way.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved high-voltage stability and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. A solid-state battery comprising the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent butyl butyrate. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The Li3YCl6 and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the moisture stability of the layer.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3InCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The tin content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The Li3YCl6, LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Part of the titanium in the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using acetonitrile for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The LLZO and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C in an oven. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery using the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium secondary battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
