title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The LLZO and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

2. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.
3. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 68% to 77%.
4. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
5. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 232 degrees C to 253 degrees C.
6. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C.
7. The sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

8. A method for producing the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and LiI to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.

9. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.

A method for producing the negative electrode structure of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing the ceramic ion conductor powder with the magnesium additive in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt%; pressing the mixture into a layer; and placing the lithium metal layer on the layer and applying a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa.
7. The method of claim 6, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
8. The method of claim 6, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, LATP, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state battery including the sheet are described. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LLZO, and LATP material. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

11. The method of claim 10, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the cycle life and moisture stability.

9. The method of claim 8, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
10. The method of claim 8, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

9. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa with a zinc additive. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the dendrite suppression.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance and rate capability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by atomic layer deposition. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li3YCl6. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The LATP and Li2ZrO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
claims: 1. 2. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%.
3. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
4. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
5. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers.
6. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.
7. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the solvent is at least one selected from the group consisting of xylene, heptane, anisole, toluene, and butyl butyrate.

8. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.
9. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

10. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the slurry of claim 1.
11. The solid-state battery of claim 10, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The low electronic conductivity of the LiNbO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The tensile strength is 1.2 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the high-voltage stability are improved.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the dendrite suppression and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3YCl6. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tantalum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium yttrium chloride and to a method for producing the same. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The resulting LiNbO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Hafnium-substituted NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a magnesium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 200 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of erbium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of erbium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The protective layer thickness is 40 nm to 200 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
