title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a lithium secondary battery. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin. The LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A precursor of the LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state lithium battery. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 70% after humid exposure. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and simpler handling.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. With zirconium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

6. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.3 micrometers to 1 micrometers.

8. A method for producing the oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, zirconium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
10. The method of claim 8, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
11. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

7. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein 0.58 <= x <= 0.67.

9. The method of claim 8, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
10. The method of claim 8, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.
12. The solid-state battery of claim 11, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3YCl6 and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the interfacial resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 material. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li7P3S11. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The resulting Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The orthorhombic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based lithium secondary battery is described. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The binder content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and beta-Li3PS4. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and sheet formability of the layer.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

7. The method of claim 3, wherein the reaction temperature is 23 degrees C to 32 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

2. The garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 1.4 micrometers to 4 micrometers.
3. The garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.
4. The garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
5. The garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
6. The garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 94% or more.
7. The garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.4.
8. The garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

9. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and an aluminum oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.
10. The method of claim 9, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

11. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The resulting LATP material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability and moisture stability at a lower cost.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The Li3PS4, LiF, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The LGPS and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life.
