title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The LiPON layer of 200 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same

A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage for lithium battery

The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state battery is described. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

3. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 95% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. With hafnium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The oxide particles have a core of the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The resulting LiNbO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The resulting LGPS material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The LGPS material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The mixed halogen substitution improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the solid-state battery.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
claims: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less.
2. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more.
3. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
4. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
5. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 5.3 V or more.
6. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 5, wherein the surface region comprises lithium phosphate.
7. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more.
8. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.6 micrometers to 2 micrometers.
9. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.
10. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 9, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.
11. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 92% or more.
12. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein an anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles has a thickness of 10 nm or less.
13. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
14. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers.
15. The oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

16. A method for producing the oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, tin, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.
17. The method of claim 16, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
18. The method of claim 16, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
19. The method of claim 16, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

20. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the oxide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.
21. The all-solid-state lithium battery of claim 20, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the layer has a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LATP, and Li6PS5Cl material. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

3. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.

5. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 400 mPa s to 750 mPa s.
6. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more.
7. The slurry of claim 6, wherein the release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer.
8. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
9. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
10. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the material has an activation energy for lithium ion conduction of 0.40 eV or less.
11. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more.
12. The slurry of claim 1, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 70 degrees C to 90 degrees C.

13. A method for producing the slurry of claim 1, the method comprising: applying the slurry having a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% onto a release film by a doctor blade; drying the applied slurry at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven; and peeling the dried layer from the release film and pressing it onto an electrode.
14. The method of claim 13, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
15. The method of claim 13, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
16. The method of claim 15, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

17. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer comprises the slurry of claim 1.
18. The all-solid-state battery of claim 17, further comprising a buffer layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer.
19. The all-solid-state battery of claim 17, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.
20. The all-solid-state battery of claim 17, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 16% or less is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The LLZO and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Germanium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. The oxygen content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 2.2 mS/cm or more. The oxygen substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sheet formability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved grain boundary resistance and rate performance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A precursor of the LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
claims: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.
2. The method of claim 1, wherein the precipitate is separated by filtration before the removing of the solvent.
3. The method of claim 1, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.7 mS/cm or more.
4. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 430 degrees C to 480 degrees C.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein the reacting is performed for 6 hours to 72 hours.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 12 wt% to 22.5 wt%.
7. The method of claim 1, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.
8. The method of claim 1, wherein a carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.5 wt% or less.
9. The method of claim 7, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.4 wt% or less.
10. The method of claim 3, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 4.1 mS/cm or more.
11. The method of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers to 10 micrometers.
12. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.
13. The method of claim 1, wherein the reacting is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more.
14. The method of claim 1, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 130 degrees C to 170 degrees C.
15. The method of claim 1, wherein the reaction temperature is 23 degrees C to 32 degrees C.
16. The method of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.5 micrometers to 15 micrometers.
17. The method of claim 1, wherein the reaction temperature is 20 degrees C to 35 degrees C.
18. A ceramic ion conductor produced by the method of claim 1.
19. The ceramic ion conductor of claim 18, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
20. The ceramic ion conductor of claim 18, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
