title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A lithium secondary battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.

11. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
12. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 3.3 MPa or more.

A method for producing the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the solid electrolyte powder with 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a lithium fluoride-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 500 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Glassy sulfide ion-conductive ceramic of the Li10GeP2S12 type with a germanium-depleted surface and lithium metal cell including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive ceramic for a lithium cell comprises crystallized grains of a tetragonal lithium germanium phosphorus sulfide represented by Li(10+d)Ge(1+d)P(2-d)S12, wherein 0 <= d <= 0.3, and a glassy surface layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm in which the germanium content is 50% or less of that in the grains. The ceramic is produced by amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, GeS2, and P2S5 by mechanical milling, crystallizing the amorphous powder at 500 degrees C to 560 degrees C, and quenching the powder in a stream of argon so that a germanium-depleted vitreous skin remains on each grain. The tetragonal grains give an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C, and the glassy skin, which is free of easily reducible germanium, suppresses the reductive decomposition that otherwise occurs when the ceramic contacts a lithium metal anode. The skin also lowers the hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C to 3 cm3/g or less, improving moisture stability. A lithium metal cell comprising the ceramic as the separator layer and a lithium metal anode operates for 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 without short circuit.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the cycle life is improved.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and cycle life and rate capability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The silicon content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The arsenic-free antimony content of 1 mol% to 4 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a zinc additive. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. The LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The inorganic layer is formed by solution casting to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The resulting LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The additive content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved dendrite suppression and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing P2O5. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. An ionic conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.1 to 0.55. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The solid content is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, the viscosity is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium zirconate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in anisole with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The wet film is dried at 100 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

10. The method of claim 9, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
11. The method of claim 10, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

12. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. With hafnium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
claims: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.
2. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 5 microamperes per square centimeter or less.
3. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 2, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
4. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 3, wherein the material has a true density of 1.8 g/cm3 to 5.5 g/cm3.
5. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 2, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.
6. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.
7. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
8. The oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.

9. A method for producing the oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing lithium, titanium, hafnium, and phosphate sources at a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%; calcining the mixture at 700 degrees C to 900 degrees C; and sintering the calcined powder and forming the oxidation-resistant surface region by an oxygen anneal.
10. The method of claim 9, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
11. The method of claim 9, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

12. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
13. The all-solid-state battery of claim 12, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3InCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium indium chloride, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

11. The method of claim 9, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.

5. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 56 micrometers to 120 micrometers.

7. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
8. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 7, wherein the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm.
9. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
10. The free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.45 micrometers to 4.5 micrometers.

11. A method for producing the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet of claim 1, the method comprising: kneading the ion-conductive solid powder with 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% of the binder under shear to fibrillize the binder; rolling the kneaded mixture between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C to form a film; and calendering the film to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
14. The method of claim 11, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 87% or more. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.3 MPa or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sheet of 30 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A precursor of the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The content of Li2O is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium indium chloride and to a method for producing the same. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm is provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 5 mol% gives a relative density of 92% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved cycle life compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.2 to 0.45, and a method for producing the same are provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium fluoride (LiF). The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
