6. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.4 micrometers to 1 micrometers.
7. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
8. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide.
9. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the inorganic layer comprises at least one selected from the group consisting of LiPON, LiF, Li3N, Li2O, and Al2O3.
10. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 43 nm to 67 nm.

11. A method for producing the protective layer of claim 1, the method comprising: forming the inorganic layer on the lithium metal by sputtering to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm; applying a solution containing a fluorine-containing polymer and a lithium salt onto the inorganic layer; and drying the applied solution to form the polymer layer.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and a method for producing the same are described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming an ion-conductive solid sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 130 degrees C to 170 degrees C.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
claims: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.
2. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
3. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
4. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.
5. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 4, wherein the hexachloride phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase.
6. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein a particle size distribution of the material has a D90 of 20 micrometers or less.
7. The halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein a mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used.

8. A method for producing the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 in a molar ratio corresponding to the composition; mechanochemically reacting the mixture in a sealed container; and heat-treating the reacted powder at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C under an inert atmosphere.
9. The method of claim 8, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
10. The method of claim 8, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

11. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the halide solid electrolyte of claim 1.
12. The lithium secondary battery of claim 11, further comprising a buffer layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer.
13. The lithium secondary battery of claim 12, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

6. The method of claim 5, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
7. The method of claim 5, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

9. The all-solid-state battery of claim 8, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation for lithium battery
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 phase and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a magnesium additive. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of an ion-conductive solid is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The substitution amount is 10 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more and a conductivity of 0.21 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the high-voltage stability is improved.

10. The solid-state battery of claim 7, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The dopant tantalum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and cycle life of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and LiF present at grain boundaries. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The content of Li2O is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The tin substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The resulting Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tungsten and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance.

abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tungsten and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by sputtering. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNbO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the moisture stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
claims: 1. 4. The method of claim 3, wherein the solvent is at least one selected from the group consisting of tetrahydrofuran, acetonitrile, ethyl acetate, and 1,2-dimethoxyethane.
5. The method of claim 1, wherein a carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.5 wt% or less.
6. The method of claim 1, wherein the precipitate is separated by filtration before the removing of the solvent.
7. The method of claim 1, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 530 degrees C to 580 degrees C.
8. A ceramic ion conductor produced by the method of claim 1.
9. The ceramic ion conductor of claim 8, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
10. The ceramic ion conductor of claim 9, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
11. The ceramic ion conductor of claim 10, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.

12. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises the ceramic ion conductor of claim 8.
13. The lithium secondary battery of claim 12, wherein the ceramic ion conductor layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers to 100 micrometers.
14. The lithium secondary battery of claim 13, wherein the positive electrode layer further comprises a conductive carbon in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and dendrite suppression.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.

2. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more.
3. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers to 10 micrometers.
4. The negative electrode structure of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 2 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved dendrite suppression. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved dendrite suppression.
