title: Titanium-substituted lithium yttrium bromide ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide glass ceramic solid electrolyte containing a Li7P3S11 crystal phase with controlled crystallinity and widened electrochemical window
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte is a glass ceramic in which a Li7P3S11 crystal phase is precipitated in a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix having a Li2S to P2S5 molar ratio of 70:30 and containing LiI in an amount of 3 mol% to 8 mol%. A glass obtained by mechanical amorphization of the raw materials in a planetary mill is heat-treated at 260 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 1 hour to 3 hours, just above the crystallization onset, so that the metastable Li7P3S11 phase precipitates with a crystallite size of 30 nm to 150 nm while devitrification to the low-conductivity Li4P2S6 phase is kept to 3% or less. The degree of crystallinity is 60% to 85%, the residual glassy phase deforms plastically during cold pressing, and the glass ceramic has an ionic conductivity of 4.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C with an activation energy of 0.22 eV. The iodide widens the electrochemical window on the reduction side to 1.6 V versus Li/Li+. The glass ceramic is distinguished from crystalline Li6PS5Cl or Li3PS4 powders by the presence of the vitreous phase and gives an all-solid-state battery with improved cycle life.

title: Tin-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and lithium battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The Li6PS5Cl and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state lithium battery. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.15 or less. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity and cycle life.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The content of SiS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The content of SiS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ErCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The tensile strength is 1.2 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the sheet formability and ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 3 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the sheet formability.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The resulting Li3YCl6 and LiF material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The bilayer structure improves the dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Dendrite-suppressing zinc additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The LiF and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. In the monoclinic structure, erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The resulting Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.075 or less. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The solid electrolyte provides improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A sheet of 50 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The Li3YCl6 and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A precursor of the LATP and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A precursor of the LATP and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li7P3S11. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The LLZO and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The resulting LATP and LLZO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiCoPO4. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A precursor of the LATP, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
