title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3YCl6. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li3YCl6 material. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.

8. The method of claim 7, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
9. The method of claim 7, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The grain size is 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved cycle life and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The bilayer structure improves the cycle life and dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The resulting LATP and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers after calendering. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The resulting LATP and Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and sheet formability.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2ZrO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The average thickness of the coating is 4 nm to 20 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the solid-state battery.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. The content of P2O5 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A solid-state lithium battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2WO4 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and LiF composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Lithium fluoride-rich halide interlayer protecting a lithium metal negative electrode from a sulfide solid electrolyte
abstract: A protective interlayer disposed between a lithium metal negative electrode and a sulfide solid electrolyte layer comprises a lithium fluoride-rich halide composition represented by Li(3-w)Y(1-w)Cl(6-6w)F(6w), wherein 0.1 <= w <= 0.3, in which fluoride partially replaces chloride so that the halide is thermodynamically stable against metallic lithium while retaining an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The interlayer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers and is formed by casting a slurry of the halide powder and a fluorinated binder onto the lithium foil, or by applying a halide coating of the composition to the surface of the sulfide solid electrolyte layer facing the negative electrode. A thin LiF-rich passivation film of 5 nm to 30 nm forms spontaneously at the lithium side upon first contact and blocks electron leakage, so that the reductive decomposition of the sulfide solid electrolyte is suppressed and the electrochemical window of the cell is extended on the reduction side to 0 V. A lithium metal cell comprising the interlayer shows an interfacial resistance of 15 ohm cm2 or less and operates for 400 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 without short circuit.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and production method thereof
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the moisture stability of the lithium metal battery.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO and Li3PS4 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The Li3InCl6 and LiF material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The content of SiS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved dendrite suppression and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.

title: Self-supporting solid electrolyte sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. With a binder content of 0.5 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

5. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.35 wt% to 0.75 wt%.
6. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes.
7. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.
8. The free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more.

9. 10. The method of claim 9, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
11. The method of claim 9, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
12. The method of claim 9, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet of claim 1.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3YCl6 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The resulting Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved sinterability and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Zirconium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4, LLZO, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Ag-C layer of 300 nm lowers the interfacial resistance to 20 ohm cm2 or less. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved dendrite suppression and interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 4.2 mS/cm. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and sinterability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the moisture stability is improved.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the grain boundary resistance.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved high-voltage stability.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 4 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The critical current density is 1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The method gives reproducible densification and improved high-voltage stability at a lower cost.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and LLZO material. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type solid electrolyte having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte provides improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
