title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sinterability.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved sinterability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved moisture stability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on titanium-free NASICON-type oxide and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.49 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the lithium secondary battery. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.4 to 0.85. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state lithium battery. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The sintered body has a relative density of 95%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sheet formability and cycle life.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by atomic layer deposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The low electronic conductivity of the LiF and Li3YCl6 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 150 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

8. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the crystal phase has an average crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm.

11. The solid-state battery of claim 9, further comprising an intermediate layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer.
12. The solid-state battery of claim 9, wherein the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability.
claims: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.
2. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.

6. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 5, wherein the powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity.
7. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
8. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 7, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.
9. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 380 degrees C to 430 degrees C.
10. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the hydrolysis of the sulfide is suppressed such that the pH of water in contact with the powder remains 10 or less.
11. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
12. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 2 cm3/g or less.
13. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
14. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 2.8 mol% to 4.1 mol%.
15. The moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 2.4 mol% to 4.5 mol%.

16. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and a tin source at a substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.
17. The method of claim 16, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
18. The method of claim 17, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
19. The method of claim 16, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
20. The method of claim 16, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
21. The method of claim 16, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
22. The method of claim 16, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and Li3YCl6 material. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The additive content is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life without a thick protective layer.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and LLTO material. A precursor of the LLZO and LLTO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Sintering at 1230 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 5 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li3PS4 material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.

title: Tin-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 200 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3YCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved interfacial resistance and Coulombic efficiency.

2. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of particles having a BET specific surface area of 1 m2/g to 20 m2/g.
3. The protective layer of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
4. The protective layer of claim 3, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
5. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 550 cycles or more.
6. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 99.5% or more.
7. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein a content of carbon in the material is 0.5 wt% or less.
8. The protective layer of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.

11. A method for producing the protective layer of claim 1, the method comprising: forming the inorganic layer on the lithium metal by solution casting to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm; applying a solution containing a fluorine-containing polymer and a lithium salt onto the inorganic layer; and drying the applied solution to form the polymer layer.
12. The method of claim 11, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
13. The method of claim 11, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
14. The method of claim 11, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
15. The method of claim 11, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

16. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein at least one of the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer comprises the protective layer of claim 1.
17. The all-solid-state battery of claim 16, wherein the battery is pressed at a pressure of 1 MPa to 20 MPa during operation.
18. The all-solid-state battery of claim 16, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.
19. The all-solid-state battery of claim 16, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiTaO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

5. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.
6. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
7. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 430 degrees C to 470 degrees C.

9. The positive electrode active material of claim 8, wherein a particle size distribution of the material has a D90 of 20 micrometers or less.
10. The positive electrode active material of claim 9, wherein the coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles.
11. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
12. The positive electrode active material of claim 1, wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.
13. The positive electrode active material of claim 12, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.

14. A method for producing the positive electrode active material of claim 1, the method comprising: preparing a coating solution containing a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate; applying the coating solution to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed; and heat-treating the coated core particles at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
15. The method of claim 14, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
16. The method of claim 14, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.
17. The method of claim 14, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
18. The method of claim 14, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.

An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed between the positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises the positive electrode active material of claim 1.
20. The all-solid-state battery of claim 19, wherein the positive electrode layer comprises a lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide.
21. The all-solid-state battery of claim 19, further comprising a buffer layer disposed between the negative electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer.
22. The all-solid-state battery of claim 21, wherein the battery is a laminate cell comprising at least two unit cells stacked in series.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.

2. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material is stored in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
3. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.
4. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers.
5. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the sintered body has a grain boundary resistance that is 20% or less of the total resistance.
6. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein a lithium ion transference number of the material is 0.99 or more.
7. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material is in the form of a powder, a pellet, or a sheet.
8. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material has a water content of 0.5 wt% or less as measured by Karl Fischer titration.
9. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, further comprising a binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt%.
10. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more.
11. The garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein an electronic conductivity of the material at 25 degrees C is 1 x 10^-8 S/cm or less.

12. A method for producing the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: calcining a mixture of Li2CO3, La2O3, ZrO2, and a tantalum oxide with a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol% to obtain a mother powder; pressing the mother powder into a pellet; and sintering the pellet at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C while covering it with the mother powder to suppress lithium volatilization.
13. The method of claim 12, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
14. The method of claim 12, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
15. The method of claim 14, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.
16. The method of claim 12, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
17. The method of claim 12, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
18. The method of claim 12, wherein a cooling rate after the heat treatment is 1 degrees C per minute to 10 degrees C per minute.
19. The method of claim 12, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium bromide ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium indium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 5.5 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved sinterability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material comprises Li3YCl6, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for producing the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and a method for producing the same are described. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and electrochemical window.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 60% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The tin substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1200 degrees C, and the resulting density is 94%. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
