title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and Li3YCl6 material. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The solid electrolyte shows improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Germanium-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved moisture stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. An ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Specific examples are Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiNbO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The slurry has a solid content of 70 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ion-conductive solid does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: A wet film of a ceramic ion conductor cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LATP material. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the lithium secondary battery without a drying step. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on perovskite-type LLTO and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The low electronic conductivity of the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The LGPS material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for an all-solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte comprises a lithium metal layer, a solid electrolyte layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The critical current density is 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the solid-state cell.
claims: 1. 9. The method of claim 8, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.
10. The method of claim 9, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
11. The method of claim 8, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
claims: 1. 9. The method of claim 8, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
10. The method of claim 8, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

9. A method for producing the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid of claim 1, the method comprising: mixing Li2S, P2S5, and an oxygen source at a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%; amorphizing the mixture by mechanical milling in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower; and heat-treating the amorphized mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere.
10. The method of claim 9, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.
11. The method of claim 9, wherein the raw materials have a purity of 99% or more.
12. The method of claim 9, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
13. The method of claim 9, wherein the mixing is performed in a planetary mixer for 10 minutes to 120 minutes.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, the porosity is 16% or less, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sheet formability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Examples of the ion conductor include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tungstate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The high coverage of the coating results in improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance and sheet formability of the layer.

10. The method of claim 8, wherein the inert gas atmosphere is argon or nitrogen.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

3. The sulfide ceramic ion conductor of claim 1, wherein the median particle diameter D50 is 1.5 micrometers to 15 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. The Li3PS4 and LATP material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. With the additive in an amount of 1 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A solid-state battery using the layer shows improved cycle life and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The oxidation potential is 5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The LATP and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The binder content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using an indium-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and the critical current density is 2 mA/cm2. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved moisture stability and operates at a lower stack pressure.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2ZrO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 20% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved moisture stability.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on NASICON-type LATP and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The germanium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the electrochemical window in contact with lithium.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The resulting Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The Li7P3S11, LLZO, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 5 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: An argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. Firing is performed at 450 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x). The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the grain boundary resistance.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The sheet thickness is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, the porosity is 20% or less, and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm or more. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The content of Li2O is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved sinterability.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a ceramic ion conductor sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 2 MPa and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4, LATP, and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved ionic conductivity.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa with a zinc additive. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
