title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
claims: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.
2. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the material is substantially free of a liquid component.
3. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 305 degrees C to 340 degrees C.
4. The sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, wherein the content of GeS2 is 4 mol% to 7.5 mol%.

5. A method for producing the sulfide solid electrolyte of claim 1, the method comprising: melting or mechanically amorphizing a mixture of Li2S, P2S5, and GeS2 to obtain a vitreous precursor; quenching the precursor to obtain a glass; and heat-treating the glass at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours to precipitate the crystal phase.
6. The method of claim 5, wherein the method is performed in an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower.
7. The method of claim 5, wherein the heat treatment is performed for 1 hour to 10 hours.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The substitution amount is 3 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. The low electronic conductivity of the LLTO, LLZO, and LATP material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. Firing is performed at 550 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The mixed halogen substitution improves the cycle life and electrochemical window of the solid-state lithium battery.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved cycle life and rate capability.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.8 MPa or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A sheet of 20 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A precursor of the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The content of GeS2 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. A precursor of the LLZO, Li3PS4, and LiF material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved cycle life.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and LiF material. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 5 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5%. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state lithium battery. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which silver is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% to suppress dendrites. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 3 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 300 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a ceramic ion conductor layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 100 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-5 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved cycle life.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP solid electrolyte in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The Li7P3S11, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl acetate for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ion-conductive solid in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF). The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Heat treatment at 250 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte shows improved moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 97% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li3InCl6, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the electrochemical window is improved.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.6 micrometers to 6 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the cycle life.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.

title: Germanium-substituted NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V
abstract: Provided is a NASICON-type LATP ceramic ion conductor in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. With germanium substitution of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The resulting LiNbO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The content of P2O5 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The content of P2O5 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which titanium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium bromide framework. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the interfacial resistance.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 85%. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl acetate at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state battery. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.

2. The method of claim 1, further comprising pulverizing the product to a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a magnesium additive. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more. Specific examples are Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a ceramic ion conductor with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 material. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The tin content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the interfacial resistance.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The tin content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the moisture stability are improved.
